metricDefs.label: Acquisitions ÷ operating cash flow
metricDefs.description: Share of the cash the business generated that went into buying companies.
metricDefs.formula: Cash paid for acquisitions minus cash from selling businesses, all years added up, ÷ operating cash flow, all years added up. A net seller shows 0%.

metricDefs.label: Free cash flow per share, growth per year
metricDefs.description: Whether each share earned more cash over time.
metricDefs.formula: Free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital spending. Divide by diluted shares. Average yearly growth from the first year to the last.

metricDefs.label: Revenue growth per year
metricDefs.description: How much bigger the company got.
metricDefs.formula: Average yearly growth in revenue from the first year to the last.

metricDefs.label: Share count change
metricDefs.description: Whether owners were diluted by new shares.
metricDefs.formula: Diluted shares in the last year ÷ diluted shares in the first year − 1. Positive means new shares were issued.

metricDefs.label: Return on capital (free cash flow)
metricDefs.description: Cash earned on all the money invested in the company, including what it paid for acquisitions.
metricDefs.formula: Last year's free cash flow ÷ average of (debt + equity) at the start and end of that year.

metricDefs.label: Net debt ÷ EBITDA
metricDefs.description: How many years of operating profit it would take to pay off the debt.
metricDefs.formula: (Debt − cash) at the last year-end ÷ average EBITDA of the last 3 years. EBITDA = profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization. Negative means more cash than debt.

metricDefs.label: Organic growth (company-reported)
metricDefs.formula: Taken as reported by the company, latest year. Not scored, because only some companies report it.

rules.result: Passes: both must-pass checks pass, and at least 75% of the other checks with data pass (3 or more with data). Fails: a must-pass check fails, or fewer than 50% pass. Mixed: anything else. Missing data is never counted as a fail.
rules.weight: 15% of the index is split equally among the companies we add, at most 8.2% each. CSU and TOI share one slot (one controls the other).
